sections.h2: What does the York County Recorder of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds records and keeps every real estate document in York County, Pennsylvania. It also records military discharge papers and notary bonds and commissions. The recorder is an elected position with a four-year term.

The office takes documents by mail, in person and through approved e-recording vendors. A seller whose title company uses e-recording never has to mail the deed. A seller who does mail it should send a check or cash for the exact fee, because the office does not take e-checks at its counter.

Indexing follows set rules. Every name variation on a document (a former name, a trading name, an also-known-as) is indexed, and the office may cross-index documents such as affidavits and rights of way so that each person or entity appears as both grantor and grantee. Where Mortgage Electronic Registration Systems acts as nominee for a lender, only that name is indexed, not the lender behind it. A title searcher reading a York County chain of title should expect those conventions.

Another service worth knowing about is the Records Alert program, which tells a homeowner when any document is recorded against their property. The county posted a notice that anyone who enrolled before May 1, 2026 has to create a new subscription in the current system, since earlier sign-ups no longer work.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in York County?
sections.html:
A deed costs $86.25 to record, and so does a mortgage or a quitclaim deed. That base covers four pages and four names. Pages past four add $2 each, names past four add $0.50 each, and every parcel identification number on the document adds $20 (the parcel charge has applied since January 1, 2025).

The county also notes that its Access to Justice fee changed to $41.25 on November 14, 2025, so use the county's fee calculator (choose York) or the printable worksheet rather than adding figures from memory.

York County recording base fees (source: York County Recorder of Deeds fee page)
DocumentBase fee
Deed, mortgage or quitclaim deed$86.25
Deed of dedication$71.25
Release of mortgage, easement, lease or assignment of mortgage$59.75
Affidavit, power of attorney or plain release$18.50
Statement of Value (transfer tax form)$2
Military discharge (DD-214)Free

Payment can be cash, a business check, a personal check or a money order made out to the Recorder of Deeds. A returned check carries a $50 service fee. Overpayments under $10 are kept, and a check that overpays by more than $10 is sent back for the right amount.

sections.h2: What must a York County deed include to be recorded?
sections.html:
The recorder's requirements sheet lists the points that most often cause a rejected deed. Check each before the closing agent sends it in:

  • The document must concern real estate, carry original signatures, and be properly notarized, in English or with an English translation.
  • A Uniform Parcel Identifier must appear on the document, with the property location (not a street address) beneath it at the top left. The county assessment office at 717-771-3253 or 717-771-4656 can supply it.
  • The grantor's name has to match the name on the prior deed exactly, so John Allen Smith cannot become John A. Smith.
  • The deed needs a precise address, because the assessment office uses it to mail tax bills.
  • The municipality, whether township, borough or city, belongs above the legal description.
  • The date on the deed must be the same as or earlier than the acknowledgment date.

When land lies in several municipalities, the deed must state the percentage split for local transfer tax. A family transfer where no tax is paid should say so in a typed statement on the deed. The Common Level Ratio factor is chosen by the date the document was signed and notarized, and the recorder's office at 717-771-9608 can supply factors for earlier years.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax when selling a house in York County?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania charges a state realty transfer tax of 1 percent of the value transferred. The Department of Revenue says the county recorder collects it together with any local transfer tax and sends the state's share on.

The local share depends on the township or borough and the school district, which is why the deed must state each municipality. Ask the recorder or your closing agent for the local rate that applies to the specific parcel before you set a net-proceeds number. The grantor and grantee are jointly liable for the tax, though who pays it is a matter of the sales contract.

The state lists several exemptions: certain transfers among family members, transfers to governmental units, deeds to burial sites, and property passed by will or intestacy. A Statement of Value is required whenever the price paid is not the full market value. An easement needs one as well, unless a public utility holds it.

sections.h2: How do I find or copy a deed in York County?
sections.html:
Documents recorded in York County are public records, except military discharges. You can search free on the public computers in the Recorder's office during open hours, and printing costs $0.50 a page. Certified copies add $1.50 per document.

To search from home you need the deed book and page. Look up the owner's name in the county's real estate assessment database and the record book and page appear under the owner record. Documents can then be retrieved online through the Landex public records link on the county site. For anything recorded before 1944, the county points researchers to the IQS site, where searching as a guest is free and printing is $0.80 a page.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about York County itself?
sections.html:
York County sits on the Susquehanna River in south central Pennsylvania, with the Mason-Dixon line as its southern edge. It covers 911 square miles and was created in 1749 from part of Lancaster County. The county holds 72 municipalities: the City of York, 36 boroughs and 35 townships. The city of York is the county seat, and Hanover was the second largest community in the 2010 census.

The economy mixes farm country with manufacturing. Snack and food producers, a Harley-Davidson plant, HVAC maker York International and York Barbell are all tied to the county. In the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate York County had 473,197 residents, up 3.7 percent since 2020.

  • Housing units: 193,394.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 76.3 percent for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $248,600.
  • Median household income: $84,829.
  • Median gross rent: $1,193.

At the median value, the 1 percent state tax alone is $2,486, and the local share comes on top of that. Sellers who inherited a house should also check the Pennsylvania inheritance tax rules before listing.

faqs.a: Yes. York County takes recordings by mail, in person and through e-recording partners approved by the county. The recorder's counter does not accept e-checks, so fees paid in the office must be by cash, check or money order.

faqs.q: What is the base fee to record a deed in York County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $86.25 for a deed, mortgage or quitclaim deed. It covers four pages and four names, and each parcel number on the document adds $20. Use the county's fee calculator to include every add-on.

faqs.q: Do I need a parcel identifier to record a deed in York County?
faqs.a: Yes. A Uniform Parcel Identifier is required on all documents before they are recorded. The assessment office can provide it. The property's location, not just its mailing address, goes beneath the UPI at the top of the deed.

faqs.q: Can I stop someone from recording a document against my York County property?
faqs.a: The Records Alert service is meant to let a homeowner know before any document is recorded against their property. Anyone who signed up before May 1, 2026 must enroll again in the new system.

faqs.q: Is there a free way to look up a York County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Public computers in the Recorder's office offer free searching during open hours, with $0.50 per printed page. Remote access runs through the county's Landex link, and the IQS site covers records before 1944 at $0.80 a page.
